proposals.name: Central Lake Public Schools Sinking Fund Millage Proposal
proposals.description: Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Central Lake Public Schools, Antrim County, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed .4766 mill ($.4766 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 4 years, 2027 to 2030, inclusive, to create a sinking fund for the purchase of real estate for sites for, and the construction or repair of, school buildings; for school security improvements; for the…
proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Central Lake Public Schools, Antrim County, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed .4766 mill ($.4766 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 4 years, 2027 to 2030, inclusive, to create a sinking fund for the purchase of real estate for sites for, and the construction or repair of, school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the acquisition of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used for the maintenance of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of eligible trucks and vans used to carry parts, equipment, and personnel for or in the maintenance of school buildings; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used to maintain such trucks and vans; and all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $203,421?
proposals.officialTitle: Central Lake Public Schools Sinking Fund Millage Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 0.4766 mills for 4 years — this is a tax increase.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.
proposals.conservativeView: This is new taxation. Ask whether the need could be met within existing budgets, whether the millage sunsets, and who oversees how the money is spent.
proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.

proposals.name: Charlevoix Public Schools Operating Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Charlevoix Public Schools, Charlevoix and Antrim Counties, Michigan, be…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Charlevoix Public Schools, Charlevoix and Antrim Counties, Michigan, be increased by 3 mills ($3.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 2 years, 2027 and 2028, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 0.1981 mill is levied in 2027 is approximately $145,463 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore that reduction)?
proposals.officialTitle: CHARLEVOIX PUBLIC SCHOOLS OPERATING MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 18 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

proposals.name: Boyne Falls Public School Operating Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law. The remaining 4 mills are only available to be levied to restore millage lost as a reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will only be levied to the extent necessary to restore that reduction.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law. The remaining 4 mills are only available to be levied to restore millage lost as a reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will only be levied to the extent necessary to restore that reduction.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Boyne Falls Public School, Charlevoix and Antrim Counties, Michigan, be increased by 22 mills ($22.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 12 years, 2026 to 2037, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 18 mills are levied in 2026 is approximately $3,552,662?
proposals.officialTitle: BOYNE FALLS PUBLIC SCHOOL OPERATING MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 18 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

proposals.name: Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle Educational Service District Special Education Millage Renewal Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will allow the intermediate school district to continue to levy special education millage previously approved by the electors.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 0.6231 mill ($0.6231 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle Educational Service District, Michigan, to provide funds for the education of students with a disability, be renewed for a period of 6 years,…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the intermediate school district to continue to levy special education millage previously approved by the electors.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 0.6231 mill ($0.6231 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle Educational Service District, Michigan, to provide funds for the education of students with a disability, be renewed for a period of 6 years, 2027 to 2032, inclusive; the estimate of the revenue the intermediate school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $2,992,734 from local property taxes authorized herein (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy)?
proposals.officialTitle: Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle Educational Service District Special Education Millage Renewal Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 0.6231 mills for 6 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.
